## CAP-STOP — line trigger crossed

`git diff --numstat` at the checkpoint measures **1,564 changed
source/test lines** (mechanism.rs 992 + r5_36.rs 498 + facts.rs +66/−7
+ lib.rs 1 + compliance/vetoes/s5_3 constructor seqs ~8) vs the
contract's **≤850 split trigger**. STOPPED before PR/close per the cap
discipline; the checkpoint commit lands the complete, green slice for
the scoped ruling.

**Proposed ruling — AMEND (recommended).** The §4.2 table is one
registry: its 21 declared metrics share the window machinery
(`deliveries`, `stop_of`, `in_window`, `subject_stop_seq`), the typed
outcome sum, and the per-subject metrics map `detect()` emits whole.
Removing metrics to fit 850 would drop AC clauses (fidelity/fallback/
ineffective/eligible counts; missing extractor/key; no-summary;
conditional-unavailable overhead) — the "never drop ACs" rule binds.
An AMEND to ≈1,600 keeps one cohesive reviewable unit; the size is
registry rows (~330), detectors (~330), reducers/report (~180),
projections (~75) and the golden battery (~500), not sprawl.

**Alternative SPLIT seam (if ruled):** leg (a) = facts projections +
registry/types + window machinery + primaries (`reacquisition`,
`repeated_action` + retained `similarity` name) + counts +
reducers/family + their golden cells; leg (b) = the conditional
detectors (activation/fidelity/request-change/trigger/ineffective/
fallback/recall/summary/overhead/opacity) + their golden cells. The
seam is awkward — `detect()` emits the whole metrics map; leg (a)
would ship a partially-populated map or a `// leg b` stub, and AC-2's
extractor/summary cells cannot run until (b).
